_comment: The plugin's argument-validation errors, as a table instead of 15 near-identical
spec files. Each row is a (with, message) pair the plugin must actually produce.
laya-workflow bdd args-probe-check materialises a spec from each row, runs it, and
requires a non-zero exit whose output contains `must_contain`.
Measured, every row here is rejected before the plugin touches CDP, so none of
them needs a browser, a page, or the fixture server: 15 runs in ~25ms total,
against 170-300ms per probe for the four specs that do need Chrome. That is why
this lives in check.sh (which CI runs) and not in run.py (which it does not).
`source` is a substring of the throw statement in plugins/bdd/main.rhai. It is
what makes the table a gate and not a list: the checker requires every `throw` in
the plugin to be claimed by a row here or by an `elsewhere` entry with a reason,
so adding a thirteenth error message without pinning it fails the build. Delete a

rows.name: unknown_op
rows.blurb: an op nobody handles is listed back with the ops that are

rows.name: navigate_without_page
rows.source: with.target_id is required - an earlier step must open a page first
rows.must_contain: bdd.navigate: with.target_id is required - an earlier step must open a page first
rows.blurb: a page-scoped op without a page says which op is missing it

rows.name: wait_for_without_page
rows.source: with.target_id is required - an earlier step must open a page first
rows.blurb: the same guard names wait_for, not navigate

rows.name: evaluate_without_page
rows.source: with.target_id is required - an earlier step must open a page first

rows.name: assert_without_page
rows.source: with.target_id is required - an earlier step must open a page first
rows.blurb: the same guard names assert, and runs before the assertion-name check

rows.name: open_without_url
rows.blurb: open says which of its two arguments is missing

rows.name: navigate_without_url
rows.blurb: navigate checks the page before the url, so an empty url is only reported once there is a target

rows.name: wait_for_without_selector
rows.blurb: wait_for with no selector would poll for nothing and then blame the page

rows.name: evaluate_without_expression
rows.blurb: evaluate refuses rather than sending an empty expression to CDP

rows.name: release_without_target
rows.blurb: release does NOT use the shared guard, so it has no 'open a page first' advice to give - that difference is deliberate and this pins it

rows.name: assert_without_assertion
rows.blurb: assert without an assertion name cannot be checked

rows.name: assert_without_value
rows.source: bdd.assert: with.value is required for assertion
rows.must_contain: bdd.assert: with.value is required for assertion 'visible'
rows.blurb: every one of the nine assertions takes a value, and the message names which one wanted it

rows.name: equals_without_expected
rows.must_contain: bdd.assert: assertion 'equals' needs with.expected (a JSON literal)
rows.blurb: equals against nothing is not a check; it says the operand is a JSON literal

rows.name: contains_without_expected
rows.blurb: contains shares its guard with equals_text and says the type it wanted

rows.name: unknown_assertion
rows.blurb: a misspelled assertion is listed back with the nine that exist

elsewhere.why: needs a real Chrome tab that never finishes loading; there is no way to produce one from the fixture server, which serves what is asked for
the load-failure catch in _op_open, same reason as the line above; it also wraps whatever the load wait threw, so it can only be reached with a browser
a budget that expires needs a page that stays still; the wait probe asserts the budget, the selector and a poll count consistent with the budget
needs a real tab that was really closed, which is the whole point of that probe

elsewhere.covered_by: dsl/browser/bdd_assert_probe.json and the xfail scenario in bdd/features/page_smoke.feature
elsewhere.why: the assertion-mismatch path, which is the plugin's ordinary success-with-a-verdict
